basics.name: Abraham Sanchez Olea
basics.label: Senior Software Engineer — Distributed systems, .NET, cloud & LLMOps
basics.summary: Senior Software Engineer with 18+ years designing, building, and operating enterprise backend systems and distributed architectures. Core strength is taking complex, high-throughput domains—logistics, tax/compliance, GIS, health-tech, and LLM platforms—from design through production. Specializes in resilient .NET systems, event-driven microservices, multi-cloud (Azure, GCP, AWS), and LLMOps: observability for agents and workflows (Langfuse, distributed tracing) and RAG on Azure OpenAI.

work.name: GlobalLogic
work.summary: Enterprise monitoring and observability for LLM applications, LangFlow workflows, and MCP components; RAG on Azure OpenAI.
highlights: Designed a distributed observability architecture for high-throughput agent activity, workflow execution, and operational metrics.
Integrated Langfuse as the primary telemetry source (spans, events, prompts, errors) for real-time health scoring and latency trends.
Implemented structured logging, distributed tracing, and correlation IDs across microservices and AI components.
Built a RAG system on Azure OpenAI: multi-format ingestion (PDF, DOCX), chunking, metadata enrichment, vector storage, and prompt-chaining.
Delivered analytical dashboards and alerting rules for agent reliability and downtime risk.

work.name: Charger Logistics Inc.
work.summary: Senior backend engineer on transportation/logistics platforms: fleet, driver, truck, and load management.
highlights: Led microservices design for load management across multiple vendor companies.
Built LoadPosting, the service that publishes trips for rating and assignment by driver companies.
Designed Platform Science microservices consuming trailer telemetry (temperature, GPS, fuel) for real-time tracking.
Designed Nugget packages for multi-cloud AppSettings and file storage across Azure, GCP, and AWS.
Mentored and enforced technical consistency across multi-service workflow projects.

work.name: Nautius International (Freelance)
work.summary: Time Card Management System (Tides) for HR, operations, and payroll. Concurrent with Charger Logistics.
highlights: Implemented .NET 8 business logic for standard hours, overtime, additional hours, and payroll alignment.
Built Angular modules for employees and HR to view, edit, and approve time cards.
Reduced payroll processing time by automating previously manual calculations; improved accuracy and auditability.

work.name: Nagarro
work.summary: Senior Staff engineer in a global digital-product engineering organization on enterprise .NET delivery.

work.name: Dextra Technologies
work.summary: J.J. Keller account: logistics, safety, and compliance products for the US market.
highlights: Owned and supported Encompas, Keller Mobile Web Services, Keller Online, and related logistics applications.
Delivered IRS Form 2290 heavy-vehicle tax filing: client submission flow plus admin console to push or revoke filings.
Unit tests as part of feature work; Jenkins ran the suite on every check-in and blocked the build on failure.
Native Android training to contribute to Keller Mobile; ELD device integrations.

work.name: SisLogic Sistemas Lógicos
work.summary: GIS and cadastral platforms for Mexican state and municipal governments. Developer and delivery lead.
highlights: SIC (Sistema de Información Catastral) for IGECEM, Estado de México: geographic digitization, cadastral valuation, spatial operations. Rolled out across several Mexican states.
APASEO cadaster (Guanajuato): shape-file import, cartography digitization, capture forms, spatial-to-tabular binding.
Oracle Spatial, SQL Server Spatial, Map Suite, PL/SQL, T-SQL, DevExpress, .NET.

work.name: STX
work.summary: Product development, then innovation team that built the company application kernel.
highlights: E-commerce cart and conference/course scheduler (PHP, AJAX, jQuery).
Core framework for Klaymobile (formerly Poscel) and a POS app with Java applets for ticket printing.
Joomla-tied CMS used by clients such as PISA; XML/XSLT reporting; Linux bash and cron.
